data.name: Guam
data.summary: Guam applies a 'mirror' of the US Internal Revenue Code: the same rules and rates as US federal income tax, paid to Guam instead of the IRS. Long-term gains and qualified dividends are taxed at up to 20%, other income up to 37%. There is no Guam estate, gift or wealth tax. US citizens who are bona fide Guam residents file only with Guam, but stay inside US federal estate and gift tax.

regimes.name: Bona fide Guam residence (mirror code)
regimes.description: Residents are taxed by Guam on worldwide income under the Guam Territorial Income Tax, which mirrors the US Internal Revenue Code (same rules and rates, 'Guam' read for 'United States').
regimes.eligibility: Bona fide residence under IRC §937 (presence test, tax home and closer connection). Non-US citizens need US immigration status: Guam applies US immigration law.

capital_gains.summary: Capital gains are taxed under the mirrored US Code: long-term gains on assets held over one year at 0%/15%/20%, so a large gain is taxed at 20%. Short-term gains are ordinary income (top 37%).

sources.title: IRS Publication 570 (2025): Tax Guide for Individuals With Income From U.S. Territories

open_questions: Whether Guam applies a mirrored 3.8% net investment income tax (IRS Pub. 570 refers taxpayers to Guam DRT) was not confirmed.
Guam Department of Revenue and Taxation primary guidance was not opened; relies on IRS Pub. 570.
capital_gains.rate_basis: Top long-term capital gains rate of the mirrored Internal Revenue Code (20%). IRS Pub. 570: Guam's tax system is 'based on the same tax laws and tax rates that apply in the United States'. The 3.8% net investment income tax is not included: IRS says it does not directly apply to bona fide territory residents and its mirrored application is a question for the territorial tax department.
capital_gains.professional_trader: As in the US code: dealers and traders with mark-to-market elections are taxed at ordinary rates.
capital_gains.holding_period_rules: More than one year for long-term treatment (mirrored IRC §1222).
capital_gains.foreign_assets: Worldwide income; foreign taxes creditable under the mirrored foreign tax credit rules.

dividends.summary: Dividends are taxed under the mirrored US Code: qualified dividends at up to 20%, non-qualified dividends at ordinary rates up to 37%.

sources.title: IRS Publication 570 (2025): Tax Guide for Individuals With Income From U.S. Territories

open_questions: How the qualified-dividend rules apply under the mirror code to dividends from US and foreign companies was not confirmed.
dividends.rate_basis: Qualified dividend rate 20% under the mirrored IRC §1(h)(11) used for both domestic and foreign dividends; non-qualified dividends (e.g. from some non-treaty foreign companies) would be taxed at up to 37%. Under the mirror system 'United States' is read as 'Guam', so how dividends from US and foreign companies qualify was not confirmed.
dividends.withholding_outbound: Mirrored US rules: 30% statutory withholding on dividends paid to non-residents (US treaties do not apply as Guam treaties).
dividends.treaty_network: Guam has no income tax treaties of its own; US treaties do not extend to Guam. Source-country WHT on US/foreign dividends is relieved by the mirrored foreign tax credit.

sources.title: IRS Publication 570 (2025): Tax Guide for Individuals With Income From U.S. Territories

open_questions: Guam real property tax rates not researched.
wealth_tax.property_tax_note: Guam levies a real property tax on assessed value; rate not researched. A gross receipts tax applies to businesses.

inheritance.summary: Guam has no estate, inheritance or gift tax of its own; the mirror system covers income tax only. US citizens remain within the US federal estate and gift tax (added by the app); see us_citizen_notes.

sources.title: IRS Publication 570 (2025): Tax Guide for Individuals With Income From U.S. Territories
26 U.S. Code § 2209 - Certain residents of possessions considered nonresidents not citizens

open_questions: No Guam statute or DRT page confirming the absence of a territorial estate or gift tax was opened; IRS Pub. 570 only describes income tax.
inheritance.domicile_rules: US citizens: federal estate and gift tax on worldwide assets unless IRC §2209 applies (citizenship acquired solely through birth or residence in a possession). Non-US citizens domiciled in Guam are treated as non-resident aliens for US estate tax (US-situs assets only).

residency.tax_residency_test: Bona fide residence under IRC §937(a): presence test (e.g. 183 days in the territory), no tax home outside Guam, and no closer connection to the US or a foreign country. A bona fide Guam resident files only with Guam (IRS Pub. 570).

routes.name: Non-US citizens: US immigration status
routes.requirements: Guam applies US immigration law: a visa or green card is needed. A green card makes the holder a US tax resident.

sources.title: IRS Publication 570 (2025): Tax Guide for Individuals With Income From U.S. Territories
26 U.S. Code § 937 - Residence and source rules involving possessions

corporate.summary: Mirrored US corporate income tax at 21%. Guam Economic Development Authority qualifying certificates can rebate most income tax for approved investments (not researched).

sources.title: IRS Publication 570 (2025): Tax Guide for Individuals With Income From U.S. Territories

data.us_citizen_notes: A US citizen who is a bona fide Guam resident for the whole year files only with Guam and owes no separate US federal income tax (IRS Pub. 570); the Guam mirror tax has the same rates, so the income tax burden is about the same as in the US, without US state tax. US federal estate and gift tax continues to apply to US citizens born or naturalised outside Guam (IRC §2209 exception only for citizenship acquired through the possession).
